prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t truthfully pick one single “best” roofer for hail repair without knowing exactly where you are in the Denver area and seeing estimates, but I can help you find the best contractor for your situation and avoid common scams. Tell me your ZIP code and whether you already have an insurance claim, and I’ll pull together a short vetted list and help you compare estimates. Meanwhile, here’s a practical checklist you can use right away.

What to look for (must-haves)
- Proper licensing and insurance: Ask for a Colorado roofing license (if required for the job size), worker’s comp and commercial general liability insurance; get copies.
- Hail/storm repair experience: Ask how many hail repairs they’ve done in Denver and whether they handle insurance claims.
- Manufacturer certifications: GAF, CertainTeed, Owens Corning or similar — shows training and ability to offer shingle warranties.
- Written, itemized estimate: Should include tear-off vs. overlay, materials, labor, cleanup, permits, and timeline.
- Written workmanship warranty (not just the shingle manufacturer warranty).
- Local references and recent job photos: Preferably in Denver neighborhoods that saw the same storm.
- Good reviews on Google/Yelp/BBB/Nextdoor and responsiveness to follow-up.

Questions to ask every roofer
- Are you licensed and insured? Can you provide copies?
- How long have you been doing hail repairs in the Denver area?
- Are you a certified installer for the shingle brand you recommend?
- Will you meet with my insurance adjuster? Do you accept assignment of benefits? (Caution with AOBs.)
- What is included in your warranty (length and what it covers)?
- Who will supervise the project? Will subcontractors be used?
- When can you start and what is the expected completion timeframe?

Insurance and claims tips
- File your claim quickly and document damage with photos before contractor work.
- Get at least three written estimates. Use them to compare line items, not just total price.
- Don’t let a contractor pressure you into signing assignment-of-benefits (AOB) paperwork unless you fully understand it — AOBs can transfer claims control and sometimes lead to contractor/insurer disputes.
- Prefer contractors who will meet your adjuster and explain line items rather than “guaranteeing” your claim payout.
- Keep all receipts and copies of correspondence.

Red flags / warning signs
- Door-to-door storm chasers pressuring you to sign today.
- Only accepts cash or demands full payment up front.
- No business address or unclear ownership.
- Vague estimates (no line-item detail) or pushes for AOB immediately.
- Very low price far under other bids — often leads to poor materials or incomplete work.

How I can help now
- If you give your Denver ZIP code and a little detail (insurance claim open? urgent?), I can:
  - Suggest 3–5 local, well-reviewed roofers to contact (based on public review criteria and typical industry reputation).
  - Draft an email/phone script and checklist you can use when getting estimates.
  - Help compare two or three written estimates if you paste them here.

Which would you like to do next?
